title: x86-64 instruction encoding (basics)
summary: x86-64 instructions are variable-length (1-15 bytes). Structure: optional prefixes (1-4 bytes: REX, operand-size, address-size, segment, lock, repeat), opcode (1-3 bytes), ModR/M byte (1 byte: mod(2) + reg(3) + r/m(3)), optional SIB byte, optional displacement (1/2/4/8 bytes), optional immediate (1/2/4/8 bytes). REX prefix (0x40-0x4F) extends registers to 16 (r8-r15) and operand size to 64-bit.

ext.spec: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual
ext.summary: x86-64 instructions are variable-length (1-15 bytes). Structure: optional prefixes (1-4 bytes: REX, operand-size, address-size, segment, lock, repeat), opcode (1-3 bytes), ModR/M byte (1 byte: mod(2) + reg(3) + r/m(3)), optional SIB byte, optional displacement (1/2/4/8 bytes), optional immediate (1/2/4/8 bytes). REX prefix (0x40-0x4F) extends registers to 16 (r8-r15) and operand size to 64-bit.

structure.meaning: REX (0x40-0x4F), operand-size override (0x66), address-size override (0x67), segment override (0x26/0x2E/0x36/0x3E/0x64/0x65), lock (0xF0), repeat (0xF2/F3).
Bit 3 (W): 64-bit operand size. Bit 2 (R): extends ModR/M reg field. Bit 1 (X): extends SIB index. Bit 0 (B): extends ModR/M r/m or opcode reg.
mod(2 bits) + reg/opcode(3 bits) + r/m(3 bits). mod=00: memory (no disp or disp32), 01: memory+disp8, 10: memory+disp32, 11: register.
scale(2) + index(3) + base(3). Used for indexed addressing (e.g., [base + index*scale + disp]).
rax, rcx, rdx, rbx, rsp, rbp, rsi, rdi, r8-r15. Plus rip (instruction pointer), rflags (status). In 32-bit mode: eax, ecx, edx, ebx, esp, ebp, esi, edi.

ext.example_decoded: x86-64: PUSH rbp; MOV rbp, rsp (function prologue)
notes: x86-64 is the 64-bit extension of x86 (AMD64/Intel 64).
Variable-length instructions make decoding complex (need to parse prefixes, opcode, ModR/M, etc.).
x86 has condition codes (flags): ZF (zero), SF (sign), CF (carry), OF (overflow), PF (parity), AF (auxiliary carry).
x86-64 has 16 general-purpose registers (vs 8 in 32-bit mode).
